# 0060: An unpriced model is priced live from LiteLLM's feed into a cached dated record, and only then refused

Status: accepted, 2026-10-07.
Refines [0007](0007-unpriced-model-aborts-before-spend.md) (an unpriced model aborts before spend) with a lookup before the refusal.
Extends [0050](0050-prices-are-dated-records-in-usd-per-mtok-grouped-by-harness.md) and [0051](0051-long-context-is-a-tier-priced-per-call-and-records-are-curated.md) with a second writer of the same records.

## Context

A model a provider released after the last plugin release has no bundled price row.
The sweep stopped at collection (ADR 0007), and the only remedy was an `xharness_prices` line the user had to look up and type.
The rate was already published, in the same LiteLLM feed the curator reads.

The plugin's own development had the mirror problem.
A model added to the catalogue needed someone to remember to run `make prices` before its price existed.

## Decision

**Collection prices a gap live before it refuses one.** `Settings.ensure_priced` finds every matrix entry no row prices on the run's day.
It looks each one up in LiteLLM's feed by exact first-party id and by its harness's `feed_provider` from the catalogue (ADR 0059).
A host's own spelling of a model is never read as a first-party rate.

**What it finds is written as a dated record under `<cache>/pricing/`.** The record has the same format as a bundled one, rendered by the same code.
A later day closes the open cache record and carries its rows forward, exactly as the curator does.
Every stamped day still resolves to the rates it had.
The price table reads cached records after the bundled ones, so a live row only fills a gap.
A replay reads the same cache, and so re-prices a live-priced run identically.

**Whatever the feed does not price either still stops the sweep.** The existing refusal names it (ADR 0007), and nothing is written.
With no gap, nothing is fetched, so a sweep of priced models never touches the network.

**The feed's location is the `xharness_price_feed` ini key.** It defaults to LiteLLM's current feed and accepts a URL or a local path, which is how the test suite stays offline.

**One conversion, two writers.** The LiteLLM-to-row conversion and the record format moved from the curator script into `derive/feed.py`.
So the curator and live pricing cannot disagree.
ADR 0051's rules bind both.
Every published rate is modelled, and an unmodelled cost field stops the write.

**`make test` curates a new bundled snapshot when the catalogue gets ahead of the prices.** It first runs the curator with `--when-catalogue-unpriced`.
That exits at once, offline, while every catalogued model is priced, and curates a new dated record otherwise.

## Consequences

A consuming project can run a model released yesterday without editing its config, provided the catalogue knows the model.
The plugin's own suite never runs with a catalogued model the bundled records cannot price.

The cache now holds a third kind of evidence beside results and the report.
Deleting it is safe for the sweep, which re-fetches, but loses the record a replay of a live-priced run needs.

## Lens

The bundled prices are a cache of the world, not the world.
When the cache misses, look the answer up and write it down where every later reader will find it.
Refuse only when the world has no answer either, and never write down a guess.
